Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 109, verse 1–6:

(p-252) Surat al-Kafirun

There are two opinions concerning it.

One: it is Meccan. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, and the majority.

The second: it is Madinan. This was narrated from Qatadah.

Mention of the occasion of its revelation. The scholars differed on three views.

One of them: a group of Quraysh, among them al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, and al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, met al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and said: "O Abu al-Fadl, if your nephew would embrace some of our gods, we would confirm what he says and believe in his God." So al-'Abbas came to him and informed him, and this surah was revealed. Abu Salih narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

(p-253) The second: "That 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, we will not leave you until you follow our religion and we follow yours. If our affair is right, you will have taken your share of it, and if your affair is right, we will have taken our share of it.' So this surah was revealed." This was said by 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr.

The third: "That Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'If it pleases you that we follow your religion for a year, and you return to our religion for a year,' so this surah was revealed." This was said by Wahb. Muqatil and others said: this surah was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and the mockers, and none of those concerning whom it was revealed remained.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿I do not worship﴾, it is in the position of "what" (ma), but it was made to correspond to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿what you worship﴾, which are the idols. And concerning the repetition of the statement there are two views.

One: it is for emphasis of the matter and to cut off their hopes regarding it. This was said by al-Farra'. We have elaborated on this explanation in the surah [al-Rahman: 13].

(p-254) The second: the meaning is: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ in my present state, ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ in your present state, ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾ concerning what I will do in the future, and likewise you, so He negated from him and from them that in the present and the future. This applies to particular people whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed that they would not believe, as we mentioned from Muqatil. Then it is not repetition at that point. This is the view of Tha'lab and al-Zajjaj. As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿For you is your religion and for me is my religion﴾, Nafi', Hafs, and Aban from 'Asim read the "ya'" of "wa-liya" with a fatha. Ya'qub affirmed the "ya'" of "dini" in both states. This verse is considered abrogated by the scholars of tafsir by the verse of the sword.
